Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of assessment from transcript: Acute itchy, dry, cracked skin with widespread involvement consistent with a flare of eczema (atopic dermatitis) in the context of a known history; no systemic symptoms; prior response to topical steroids; OTC steroid use without relief; plan to escalate topical therapy and skin care; add antihistamines for itch; consider trigger diary to identify possible allergens or irritants; follow-up in 7–10 days if not improved
- Relevant DDx considerations incorporated:
  - Atopic dermatitis (eczema flare): High likelihood given history and presentation
  - Allergic contact dermatitis: Medium likelihood; potential exposure to new skin products; plan to diary triggers
  - Irritant contact dermatitis: Medium likelihood; possible contribution from skin washing and products
- Notes on conflicts: No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx

Management Plan
- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded: Prescribe stronger topical corticosteroid; continue/emphasize regular emollients; advise daily skin-care regimen (bath/shower emollient use for 7–10 days); recommend over-the-counter antihistamines (e.g., loratadine or diphenhydramine) with consideration of stronger option (Fexofenadine) started today; encourage keeping a diary of potential triggers (products, soaps, laundry detergents); schedule follow-up in 7–10 days to assess response; if no improvement, consider escalation or alternative therapies
